newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ/Qantas to cease "air share" agreement.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ/Qantas to cease "air share" agreement.

text.p: Air New Zealand Ltd said on Monday it would cease its "Tasman Air Share" agreement with Qantas Airways from May 1.
The agreement, introduced in 1991, boosted seating capacity and the number of flights operated by both carriers under a code-sharing arrangement.
Aircraft operated by one airline also carried the flight number of the other, with the non-operating carrier selling its allocation of seats as if they were their own.
Air share flights now represented only a small percentage of Tasman capacity for the two airlines.

The agreement had helped them ensure that Tasman routes continued to be well-served while they pursued growth markets in Asia and Japan. But Air NZ said the carriers were now at "different points in our development".
The total number of flights by both airlines across the Tasman would increase slightly, although the number of seats offered would remain about the same.
